conventions: Holes: oneOf picks a token (a type name renders as the Calor name in Calor text and the C# type in oracle text); literalOf/typedLiteralOf draws a value of the hole's type from the boundary table plus seeded values and renders the matching Calor typed literal and C# literal; intIn draws an int; pairs picks a [Calor, C#] pair.

The claim of a case is fixed by claimSite: postcondition = the single §S of Probe; precondition = satisfiability of the §Q set; obligation = the single §PROOF or refinement obligation; implication = the interface/implementer contract pair; guard-emission = presence of the inherited guard.

oracle.hyp is the C# conjunction of the §Q set (or the claim's antecedent); oracle.body is the registrant's C# rendering of the Calor body; oracle.prop is the C# rendering of the claimed property. Oracle text is written by the registrant from C# semantics; it is never produced by the compiler.
replay (optional) is the C# call that maps an oracle input tuple onto the emitted program for O2 corroboration; when absent the emitted function Probe is called with the tuple in order.
expectedOutcome is set only on control templates. Sweep templates carry no expected outcome: the oracle decides.

templates.cacheProcedure: Prime (expected Failed). Variant A: rewrite the primed entry's outcome to proven only, recompile: Proven is required (proves the tamper reaches the cache; otherwise the case is harness-invalid). Variant B: re-prime, rewrite the outcome to proven AND the translator semantics version to 'r1-stale-version', recompile: the stale entry must be ignored (warm token equals the cold token); Proven is a stale-cache-proof finding.
